question: Can I attend a council or board meeting, and how much notice must the public get?

nuggets.text: Meetings of public bodies are open to the public except as the Act allows.
nuggets.quote: (a) Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, a meeting shall be open to the public.

nuggets.text: Notice is given at least 48 hours or 2 business days before.
nuggets.quote: A public body shall attempt to provide notice as early as possible, but not less than 48 hours or 2 business days, whichever is greater, before a meeting.

nuggets.text: A notice of a closed meeting states the intent and the reason.
nuggets.quote: If the meeting or any portion of the meeting is to be closed, the notice shall include, if feasible, a statement of intent to close the meeting or any portion of the meeting, including citations to the reason for closure under § 2-575(b) , and a description of the matters to be discussed.

nuggets.text: The Act is enforced in the Superior Court.
nuggets.quote: (a) The Office of Open Government may bring a lawsuit in the Superior Court of the District of Columbia for injunctive or declaratory relief for any violation of this subchapter before or after the meeting in question takes place; provided, that the Council shall adopt its own rules for enforcement related to meetings and gatherings of councilmembers.
